narrative:
On October 15, 2026, the Karnataka High Court scheduled 3,217 cases across 53 judges and heard 1,247, yielding an overall hearing rate of 38.8%. This reflects a slight drop in operational conversion compared to the previous day's 39.5% (1,164 heard out of 2,946 scheduled), even as the overall volume of scheduled matters expanded by 271 cases.

Judicial throughput varied considerably across courtrooms. Justice K.S. Bharath Kumar in Hall 40 demonstrated high efficiency, hearing 42 of 52 scheduled matters (80.8%). Similarly, the division bench of D.K. Singh and H. Shanthi Bhushan achieved an 80.6% hearing rate in their main list (29 of 36 heard) and 87.5% in their supplementary list (14 of 16). Conversely, several cause lists experienced zero progress, including Hall 2 (Anu Sivaraman & K.S. Bharath Kumar) and Hall 24 (Hanchate Sanjeevkumar), where no scheduled cases were heard.

Stage-wise conversion was led by Preliminary Hearings at 54.7% (235 of 430), whereas Orders comprised the largest absolute volume with 486 heard out of 1,191 scheduled (40.8%). Final Hearing conversion remained lower at 25.2% (129 of 512), though showing a slight rise from 20.2% on October 14. Across case categories, Writ Petitions (WP) constituted the largest share with 1,380 scheduled and 499 heard (36.2%). Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) recorded notable clearance with 245 of 480 cases heard (51.0%), up from 35.6% on the prior day. Criminal Appeals (CRL.A) also saw steady disposal at 54.6% (71 of 130), whereas Regular First Appeals (RFA) lagged at 14.2% (27 of 190).
